basic_info: 62-year-old male with chief complaint of breathing difficulty and leg swelling for 10 days
present_illness: Onset 10 days ago, symptoms include shortness of breath, especially when walking up a flight of stairs, and bilateral leg swelling, particularly around the ankles, without pain or redness. No chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness during episodes of shortness of breath. No recent weight gain or changes in urine output. The patient reports that the shortness of breath is affecting daily activities, particularly when climbing stairs, but does not prevent him from performing routine tasks. The leg swelling is mild and has not worsened; it is primarily noted in the proximal areas and is pitting. The patient has also reported increased fatigue, especially after physical exertion.
past_history: History of type I diabetes and congestive heart failure. Medications: Insulin pump for diabetes, omeprazole for reflux. No diuretics or heart failure medications currently prescribed. Patient is unsure if any diuretics or heart failure medications were prescribed in the past. No history of renal disease, proteinuria, or other relevant comorbidities reported.
physical_exam: Vital signs: Blood pressure 140/85 mmHg, heart rate 78 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Physical examination reveals bilateral pitting edema up to the knees, no jugular venous distension, clear lung fields, and no peripheral cyanosis. Cardiac examination shows S3 gallop, no murmurs. Abdomen is soft and non-tender with no hepatomegaly. Lower extremity edema is non-pitting in the distal aspects, but pitting in the proximal areas.
aux_exam: Recent laboratory results: Serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m²), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 35 mg/g. Chest X-ray shows no cardiomegaly or pulmonary edema. Echocardiogram reveals left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 35%
